hints.title: Use the exactly-one restriction
hints.body: If one option implies another option, it cannot be the only correct option. An iff statement contains its matching if statement.
hints.recap: A stronger listed guarantee may force a second truth.
hints.pitfall: Do not assess the options as unrelated facts.
hints.pause: Which options are immediately implied by A and C?

recall.reminder: A statement that forces another listed statement cannot be the sole truth.

hints.title: Compare the input sets
hints.body: Draw the sets of inputs satisfying <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>. Determine which set is contained in the other.
hints.recap: A universal guarantee on a set also holds on each subset.
hints.pitfall: A guarantee on a smaller set says nothing about its missing inputs.
hints.pause: Decide which implication between the remaining options is forced.

recall.reminder: A universal guarantee on a set also holds on each subset.

hints.title: Test whether a unique truth is possible
hints.body: Try a statement true precisely for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo><</mo><mi>c</mi><mo><</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>. Test each option against this rule.
hints.recap: A consistency example must satisfy exactly the required number of options.
hints.pitfall: An if condition need not describe every input where the statement is true.
hints.pause: Evaluate all four options and identify the only possible sole truth.

recall.reminder: An if statement guarantees its conclusion when its premise holds; it need not describe all cases where the conclusion holds.

solution:
A implies B because an iff includes the forward if direction, so A cannot be the sole truth. Similarly C implies D, excluding C.

B says that every x>1 makes the statement true. Since every x>2 is among those inputs, B implies D. Thus B also cannot be the sole truth, leaving D.

For consistency, suppose the statement is true precisely for x>32. It is true whenever x>2, so D holds. B fails for inputs between 1 and 32, A fails for the same reason, and C fails because some inputs between 32 and 2 also make the statement true.

Answer D.
knowledgePattern: Use implications between answer options plus uniqueness of the correct option
